title: RAW hazard with pipelined wgmma and LHS in register
body:
We hit a RAW hazard when the `wgmma.mma_async` LHS operand is passed in registers.

From the [`wgmma.wait_group`](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/parallel-thread-execution/#asynchronous-warpgroup-level-matrix-instructions-wgmma-wait-group) documentation:

> Accessing the accumulator register or the input register containing the fragments of matrix A of a `wgmma.mma_async` instruction without first performing a `wgmma.wait_group` instruction that waits on a wgmma-group including that `wgmma.mma_async` instruction is undefined behavior.

Triton [inserts](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/088fbe15e4868506ac0ad42a3cfbbc923971b8d4/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Pipeliner/WGMMAPipeline.cpp#L666) a `warp_group_dot_wait` for this, which lowers to `wgmma.wait_group`. The `pendings` value (explained in [this comment](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/088fbe15e4868506ac0ad42a3cfbbc923971b8d4/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/Pipeliner/WGMMAPipeline.cpp#L657-L660)) however does not prevent the RAW hazard: `properlyAsyncDots.size() - 1` only guarantees that the first `wgmma.mma_async` has finished during the next loop iteration. As a result, dot prologue instructions may write to the input registers of the other `wgmma.mma_async` instructions from the previous iteration before they have executed.

We have only seen the issue manifest itself with an 'empty' prologue, where the results of a `ldmatrix` instruction are passed directly to `wgmma.mma_async`. If the `ldmatrix` results are first copied to another register (for example through negating the input), the issue seems to disappear. Passing the LHS input in register directly from `ldmatrix` requires a bit of a dance (see repro below), but we do see the same issue in real workloads where the `if` statement is the result of a concat.

Changing `properlyAsyncDots.size() - 1` to `0` fixes the issue, but has significant performance impact, because the `wgmma.wait_group` follows right after the `wgmma.mma_async`, instead of before the input register is written.

```
import sys
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@participant6.jit
def wgmma_register_sync_repro_kernel(
    a_ptr,
    b_ptr,
    c_ptr,
    M: tl.constexpr,
    N: tl.constexpr,
    K: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
    BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr,
):
  pid = tl.program_id(axis=0)

  offs_m = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
  offs_n = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
  offs_k = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)

  a_ptrs = a_ptr + (offs_m[:, None] * K + offs_k[None, :])
  b_ptrs = b_ptr + (offs_k[:, None] * 1 + offs_n[None, :] * K)

  acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)

  for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K):
    # Force A to be passed in register directly from ldmatrix.
    if pid >= 0:
      a = tl.load(a_ptrs)
    else:
      a = tl.load(a_ptrs)
    b = tl.load(b_ptrs)

    # This produces the following PTX code:
    # 4x ldmatrix.sync.aligned.m8n8.x4.shared.b16 {<A registers>}, [...];
    # 4x {
    #   wgmma.fence.sync.aligned;
    #   wgmma.mma_async.sync.aligned {<ACC registers>}, {<A registers>}, ...;
    #   wgmma.commit_group.sync.aligned;
    #   wgmma.wait_group.sync.aligned 3;
    # }
    # RAW hazard: the ldmatrix instructions write <A registers> before the last
    # 3 wgmma.mma_sync instructions have read them.
    acc = tl.dot(a, b, acc, out_dtype=tl.float32)

    a_ptrs += BLOCK_K
    b_ptrs += BLOCK_K

  c_ptrs = c_ptr + (pid * M * N) + (offs_m[:, None] * N + offs_n[None, :])
  tl.store(c_ptrs, acc)


def test_repro():
  torch.manual_seed(0)

  M = 64
  N = 128
  K = 4096
  BLOCK_M = 64
  BLOCK_N = 128
  BLOCK_K = 64

  NUM_BLOCKS = 512

  a = torch.randn((M, K), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
  b = torch.randn((N, K), device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16).t()
  c = torch.empty((NUM_BLOCKS, M, N), device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)

  print(
      f"Running on {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)} with {NUM_BLOCKS} blocks..."
  )

  wgmma_register_sync_repro_kernel[(NUM_BLOCKS,)](
      a, b, c, M=M, N=N, K=K, BLOCK_M=BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N=BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K=BLOCK_K
  )

  torch.cuda.synchronize()

  target = torch.matmul(a.float(), b.float())
  diff = torch.abs(c - target.unsqueeze(0))
  max_diff = torch.max(diff)

  print(f"Max Abs Error: {max_diff.item()}")

  if max_diff.item() > 1.0:
    print("FAILED: Output corrupted (Race Condition triggered).")
    sys.exit(1)
  else:
    print("PASSED: Output matches.")


if __name__ == "__main__":
  test_repro()
```

### Environment details

Triton version: 84214b6
GPU: H100

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
The problem is that we assume ptxas will schedule the LHS argument update so that instead of updating the LHS registers all in one go, it goes as:
```
wgmma_wait 1
update A[0]
wgmma acc, A[0], B[0]
wgmma_wait 1
update A[1]
wgmma acc, A[1], B[1]
```
I guess the ldmatrix somehow blocks this rescheduling.

It's unclear how we could fix this at an llvm level. You would need to ensure that `A` lives in a different set of logical registers to the LHS argument to the wgmma which requires us to somehow allocate registers in llvm which is nonsense. WGMMA is just broken from a compiler perspective.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I did some experiments with `ptxas` from CUDA 13.1 (`build cuda_13.1.r13.1/compiler.36836380_0`).

The kernel ([wgmma_register_sync_test.ptx.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25289161/wgmma_register_sync_test.ptx.txt)) doesn't perform a correct matmul, it only intends to investigate the behaviour of `ptxas`'s liveness analysis. It follows the structure of the code in my previous [comment](https://github.com/participant6-lang/participant6/issues/9433#issuecomment-3891954250).

`ptxas` maps `%a0` and `%d0`, `%a1` and `%d1` to the same physical register and then detects its own mistake:
It changes `wait_group` to `0` (`WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x0;` in [wgmma_register_sync_test_c7513.sass.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25289353/wgmma_register_sync_test_c7513.sass.txt)) and prints `(C7513) Potential Performance Loss: wgmma.mma_async instructions are serialized due to non wgmma instructions defining input registers of a wgmma between start and end of the pipeline stage in the function 'wgmma_register_sync_test' in line 0`.

So the test does not expose a correctness bug in `ptxas`. With correct code (copy `%d` to `%a` before `fence/mma_async`), it produces correct but slow code. Without the copy, it's simply garbage in, garbage out.

In order to prevent `ptxas` from mapping `%a` and `%d` to the same physical register, I manually extended the lifetime of `%a` until after the `wait_group` with extra `xor %d, %d, %a` instructions. With those, it leaves `wait_group` unchanged (`WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x1;` in [wgmma_register_sync_test_xor.sass.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25289704/wgmma_register_sync_test_xor.sass.txt)) and `C7513` goes away.

So I'm wondering, is the `ptxas` fix coming in CUDA 13.2 about correctly analyzing the lifetime of `mma_async` input registers and producing *faster* code, or is there also a correctness bug that I failed to trigger in my experiments?

I did not experiment with register ping-pong and an unrolled loop (second snippet in [this comment](https://github.com/participant6-lang/participant6/issues/9433#issuecomment-3890904677)). I assumed this is the recommended structure to work around the `ptxas` limitation, but I suspect that it would result in the same `C7513`.

```

w1, w2, ... w8 = split W_bf16 // split into 8 pieces along K dim

mov w1', w1
wgmma w1', x1, acc  // w1 is reg, x1 is smem
commit_group
wait 7

mov w2', w2
wgmma w2', x2, acc
commit_group
wait 7
.
.
.
mov w8', w8
wgmma w8', x8, acc
commit_group
wait 7
```

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
@reporter I have an update on this issue. When I said "Triton generates movs", that turned out to be true only for some workloads in the MoE test that I was looking at last year. Moreover, those movs are actually generated by LLVM from `insert / bitcast` etc in https://github.com/participant6-lang/participant6/blob/main/third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/DotOpToLLVM/WGMMA.cpp#L118-L125. Today I found that there are workloads in the MoE test for which those `insert / bitcast` are optimized away by LLVM which results in

```
LHS = ...

wait N - 1

wgmma acc, LHS, RHS
```  

rather than

```
LHS = ...

wait N - 1

reg = mov LHS
wgmma acc, reg, RHS
```  

According to @participant1, such copy propagation across `wait N - 1` by LLVM is legal. So we cannot rely on LLVM to materialize `mov` from `insert / bitcast`. Previously OAI tried such manual `mov` insertion in Triton, but due to the bug in ptxas, such trick didn't work. Now that the fixed ptxas is coming, we should revisit this. I don't know why your workload + manual mov is not affected by the ptxas bug, but it's good that you don't have to wait for the 13.2 update.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Thanks for adding these `mov`s. I've tested this change at HEAD with my repro from the top.

It looks like the `mov`s are placed after instead of before the `fence`. I've opened https://github.com/participant6-lang/participant6/pull/9530 to put them before.

With that, the PTX looks correct, but the SASS does have the RAW hazard: `R96` and `R88` (the inputs to the second set of `HGMMA`) are written before the first `WARPGROUP.DEPBAR`: [wgmma_register_sync_repro_kernel.sass.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/25444162/wgmma_register_sync_repro_kernel.sass.txt). This is with `ptxas V13.1.115`.

Given that it will likely take a while before XLA upgrades to CUDA 13.2, we will play it safe and use the `wait_group 0` [patch](https://github.com/openxla/xla/blob/main/third_party/participant6/temporary/wgmma_pipeline_fix.patch) for the time being.
